Q: Is there a "set" data structure in bash? A:

There is no definite set type but you can turn an array into an array which is a set with the _array_set function of the Crash Bash library.

_array_set \
  "<array-name>" \
  "<set-name>"

Q: Creating a tibble with specific information pulled out A:

Compare

a <- dput(head(co2, 2))
date_decimal(a) # error
date_decimal(as.numeric(a)) # as expected

Q: How can I create a set-like array in bash? A:

I've added a function implementing the other answer called _array_set and added it to the Crash Bash library, so now one to turn an array into a set one can simply write

_array_set \
  "<array-name>" \
  "<set-name>"

Q: In Python while unsing the PIL pillow library. When I open an image and call load on it do it still need to close it? A:

Thanks for replying! Yes I agree that with should be used. So if i would do:

with Image.open("some path") as image:
    image.load()

image_grayscale = image.convert("L")

image_grayscale = image = "some other thing"
# or
del image_grayscale, image

As I understand it this wouldn't cause any memory problems, right? Running it doesn't produce any errors.

The documentation in "File handling in Pillow" I am basing this on:

  • Image.Image.close() Closes the file and destroys the core image object.

    The Pillow context manager will also close the file, but will not destroy the core image object. e.g.:

    with Image.open("test.jpg") as img:
    img.load()
assert img.fp is None
img.save("test.png")

This should explain my question but I am unsure if the garbage collector will collect the "core image object". But seems like it.

Q: Curl upload command works at command line but not in script A:

Remove the outer single quotes so the command actually executes:

for file in *.gz; do
  fullfile=$(pwd)/$file
  http_code=$(curl -L -u "$1:$2" -o /dev/null -s -w "%{http_code}" \
    --upload-file "$fullfile" "https://myurl/path/$3/$file")
done
